cascade.org: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV
cascade.projectName: Connecting Power: Scaling and Sharing Sub-Granting Experiences to Prevent and Combat Gender-Based Violence Across Europe
cascade.furtherInfo:
The CoPower project is implemented by Oxfam Italia ETS, Action Aid Hellas, Asociación Bienestar y Desarolloa and We World-GVC. It started on 1 March 2026 and will end on 28 February 2029.
 Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of Civil Society Organisation (CSOs) to provide safe and inclusive services for victims of gender-based violence (GBV) against women, girls, and children in all their diversity across six European countries: Italy, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Romania, and Albania.
 The project foresees three national calls, along with transnational calls involving the following country pairs: Italy–Serbia, Spain-Romania, and Greece-Albania. The national calls will fund at least 10 projects in Italy, 10 in Spain and 10 in Greece. The transnational calls will fund 5 projects for Italy and Serbia, 5 projects for Spain and Romania and 5 projects for Greece and Albania. Overall, a minimum of 60 CSOs will be engaged, fostering meaningful cross-country cooperation.
 A comprehensive capacity-sharing programme for CSOs will include needs assessments, training, mentoring, and both national and international workshops to promote mutual learning and support in the full implementation of the EU Violence Against Women Directive.
cascade.howTo:
The CoPower Action has been designed to directly fund initiatives addressing Gender Based Violence(GBV) against women, girls and children through an intersectional approach .
 All eligible activities supported through the project calls will directly respond to the multidimensional and intersecting needs of women, girls, and child survivors of GBV, strengthening an inclusive and accessible protection systems across different intervention contexts. Child protection and gender mainstreaming are expected to be integral components of the proposals submitted by CSOs, while partner organisations will provide dedicated technical support to improve the capacities of participating CSOs in these areas.

 Three national calls will support CSOs in Italy, Greece and Spain focusing on: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV . 
 TARGET APPLICANTS  
 The calls target small and medium-sized grassroots CSOs , particularly those operating in rural, peripherical or marginalised areas and legally registered in Italy, Greece or Spain. The primary target group, will include Women’s rights organisations (WROs), Anti-violence centres and anti-trafficking centres, Human rights, LGBTIQ+ rights, child rights, social inclusion and disability, elderly, migrant and refugee organisations. 
 2 FUNDING WORKSTREAMS:  
 1. Enhanced protection response for women, girls and children, victims of GBV, adopting an intersectional approach. This area focusses on providing tailored protection and support services, including safe houses, medical and psychological assistance for women and girls, in all their diversity, who are victims of domestic, sexual violence and other forms of GBV considering specific barriers for equal access to protection (Budget: 540,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 
 2. Reduction of harmful practices , with a focus on improving interventions against harmful practices such as female genital mutilation, intersex genital mutilation

 The objective of the call is to support co-creation between Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations and their peers from Creative Europe countries on the topic of resilience.
 Funding will be available for co-creation projects involving at least one Ukrainian partner and a partner from another Creative Europe participating country. Each partner is expected to play a role of comparable weight in the project — whether through creative input, management responsibilities, or audience development. All creative sectors are eligible, with the exception of the audio-visual sector. Each co-creation project must include a public presentation in the locality of every participating partner.
 Purpose of the call: 
 - To develop and present an international co-creation on the topic of resilience, in any artistic/cultural sector except audio-visual.
- To carry out at least two local presentations (one/locality, including in Ukraine)
 Budget: 
 — Total funding available 187,500€
 — Amounts per grant: Up to 25,000€, covering up to 90% of project costs.
 — Applicants are expected and required to provide the rest of the total project budget as a contribution.

cascade.howTo:
Perform Europe is a funding scheme offering EUR 1.4 million for performing arts collaborations across all 41 Creative Europe countries. Perform Europe supports partnership proposals which reinvent the way we tour across borders.
 The highly successful Perform Europe pilot (2020–2022) and second edition (2023–2026), was coordinated by a Consortium of six organisations; five major performing arts networks, IETM - International network for contemporary performing arts, European Festivals Association (EFA), European Dance Development Network (EDN), Circostrada, Pearle* - Live Performance Europe together with the research organisation IDEA Consult.  
 Co-funded by the European Union, Perform Europe has granted a total of €3.5 million to 61 cross-border macro-projects involving 272 partners. Together, they have toured over 80 artistic works across 41 countries, reaching new audiences and testing innovative approaches to inclusion, sustainability and cooperation.
 Building on these achievements, the third and final edition of Perform Europe under the current Creative Europe programme (2021-2028) will continue to explore, together with the performing arts sector, how cross-border touring can become fairer, greener and more inclusive, while further consolidating the knowledge, partnerships and practices developed through the programme. 
 By the end of this third edition, Perform Europe will have supported at least 86 cross-border touring projects in total, building a substantial body of experience and knowledge that continues to strengthen the European performing arts ecosystem.

cascade.howTo:
GreenChips-EDU Scholarship 
 1. Purpose of the call 
 The GreenChips-EDU Project was launched in 2023 with the aim of supporting talents in sustainable semiconductor technologies across Europe. The project seeks to educate students and researchers, equipping them with knowledge that will contribute to eco-friendly chip design, energy-efficient manufacturing, and materials innovation for the future of the EU.
 As part of this initiative, TU Graz is pleased to announce a call for applications for scholarships supporting Master’s students enrolled or planning to enroll in the relevant study programmes at TU Graz :
 - Electrical and Electronics Engineering
- Information and Computer Engineering
- Biomedical Engineering
 The scholarship is intended to provide financial support to students participating in academia-industry collaborations through mobility programmes . The goal is to foster cooperation between academia and industry and enrich the educational experience of students dedicated to advancing sustainable and innovative technologies in the electronics and microelectronics sectors.
 2. Type of grants 
 The eligible expenses outlined in this document must be directly related to international and domestic mobility activities carried out at partner institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. These mobility activities may also take place at industrial partner sites, including those that are not formal project partners, provided they align with the project's objectives and offer meaningful academic or professional engagement. In such cases, the mobility may take the form of professional training, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop practical skills within relevant industry settings.

records.description:
About Phortify 
 Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.
 About the Phortify Funding Framework 
 Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

records.description:
This support scheme is launched to support and facilitate Master students to take part in educational activities external to their own organization. It allows Master students to participate in fusion Master classes, summer schools, and other short-term events with a dominant educational character. All conferences are excluded from support except when the Master student has his/her own contribution at the event (see terms and conditions for details).
 Students registered at universities that are a  FuseNet member  and/or are seeking to attend educational activities at hosts that are a  FuseNet member , and both the home university and the educational event are located in one of the countries that are part of the  EUROfusion member states , can apply here for financial support to take part in a fusion-related educational training activity.
 The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and subsistence support (depending on the duration). The (training) activity has to take place at a university group or research institute in one of the EUROfusion members states or at a FuseNet member institute. The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before the actual start of the educational event. The educational event has to start no later than 6 months after application.

records.description:
Open Internet Stack is an initiative by the European Commission to work towards an resilient operational stack of strategic technology commons worthy of trust — a stable and defendable foundation to foster healthy and strong democracies and economies, delivering the European vision of next generation digital infrastructures and connected collaborative computing networks. It aims to deliver an ecosystem of deployable, scalable, and secure technologies that allow for permissionless innovation, contribute to quality of life and deliver strategic autonomy.
 The goal of Restack is to help deliver, mature and scale new internet commons across the technology stack: from libre chips to middleware without a vendor lock-in, from productivity tools to 'local-first' infrastructure — and of course the end user applications needed to consume those networked services. We restack because there is no other viable way. If we want to reclaim digital self-sustainability and yield the full benefits from technology as a society, we need to have an entire stack that is open from the ground up — period.
 Only though enough critical mass of shared building blocks and collective pooling of resources and capabilities will our governments, businesses and civil society be able to count on digital security and long term operational availability — and steer towards more fair, innovative economies and societies. And there is no time to waste. This is why we invite your contribution to help us reshape the state of play, and together create an open, trustworthy and reliable internet for all.
 This is your opportunity to make a real difference . In order to enable you to make such contributions, we will award small to medium-size R&D grants towards solutions that bring the next generation of mobile solutions closer. We are seeking project proposals between 5.000 and 50.000 euro's — which should get you on your way. if there is proven potential, there is a possibility to subsequently scale up your project significantly. Next to financial support, we provide all kinds of help too — ranging from accessiibility scans and security audits to reproducible packaging, and from support with copyright compliance and governance to standardisation.

records.description:
Open data about software packages is critical for the automation and scale necessary to resolve software supply chain management and address security and regulatory and open source compliance challenges. CodeSupply aggregates and curates comprehensive software metadata, including origin and licensing information, security vulnerabilities, and quality metrics from distributed, authoritative data sources across programming ecosystems and software types. This metadata is assembled in reference data sets, federated in a unified data catalog for digital sovereignty and independence, and distributed as open data, freely available to all, using an open source data license.
 The CodeSupply project pursues three interconnected objectives that directly address data challenges in cybersecurity, software supply chain management, and regulatory and open source license compliance:
 - Publish current, correct, and comprehensive software metadata 
- Establish a scalable and sustainable mechanism to provide democratic access to data sets
- Create a foundational framework for future iterations, enhancements, and new data sets
 CodeSupply will deliver an ambitious development effort, but this is a vast domain with many more challenges than what any preconceived effort could tackle by itself. This is why we invite your contribution to help us reshape the state of play, and together create an open, trustworthy and reliable internet for all.
 This is your opportunity to make a real difference . You tell us how your project can help CodeSupply go harder, better, faster, stronger. In order to enable you to make such contributions, we will award small to medium-size R&D grants towards solutions that bring the next generation of mobile solutions closer. We are seeking project proposals between 5.000 and 50.000 euro's — which should get you on your way. If the project works out well you can subsequently scale up in other programmes funded by NLnet such as Restack . Noteworthy fact: several projects within CodeSupply were themselves bootstrapped on precisely such a grant from NLnet, and now it is your turn.

 BiodivFuture focuses on supporting future-looking research and innovation that will address biodiversity and novel ecosystems, as well as their socio-ecological dynamics and consequences relating to the sustainability goals of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and associated future pathways and trajectories of change. The call covers investigating the causes (drivers), effects (biological responses), and outcomes (including opportunities, risks and trade-offs) of current and future trajectories of change in all relevant realms (terrestrial, freshwater, marine and coastal areas), in all regions of the world . It aims at funding novel, high-quality transnational research with potential for societal and political impact that will significantly improve our understanding of novel ecosystems with holistic, systemic, and integrated approaches.
 In the face of inevitable and potentially irreversible change, knowledge generated under this call should ultimately lead to actions to achieve impacts that sustain resilient, interconnected, diverse and ecologically functioning ecosystems. This could include critical reflection on what constitutes ecosystem states that best preserve or restore natural resources by taking multiple costs and benefits (trade-offs) into account and the diversity of contexts, scales, perspectives and world views. records.description:
The FOREST Joint Call 2026 – ForestPathways supports transnational research and innovation activities across the spectrum from fundamental research to applied research and, where appropriate, demonstration activities. Projects are expected to generate new knowledge, develop practical solutions, and contribute to implementation in policy, management or industry contexts, while considering the diversity of forests and the forest-based sector.
 Applicants must select the single topic that best reflects the primary focus of their proposal. Proposals may address multiple topics but will be evaluated and ranked under one primary topic.
 TOPIC 1 – Climate-Resilient Forest Systems: “How forests function and respond to climate change” 
 This topic supports research and innovation addressing the resilience, adaptive capacity, and long-term sustainability of forest ecosystems under changing environmental conditions, including climate change and increasing disturbance pressures. It aims to strengthen the scientific basis for climate-resilient forest systems and support their adaptation and mitigation to climate change, within broader environmental and socioeconomic contexts.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, carbon dynamics measurement, monitoring and assessment of carbon stocks and sinks; adaptation pathways and strategies; forest ecosystem processes and dynamics; disturbance regimes, including wildfires and other abiotic and biotic disturbances, pests and diseases; landscape-level interactions and spatial dynamics; and genetic diversity and adaptive capacity, including assisted migration.
 TOPIC 2 – Adaptive and Multifunctional Forest Management Systems: “How forests should be managed under changing conditions” 
 This topic supports research and innovation focused on the implementation of adaptive and multifunctional forest management systems that enhance resilience, sustainability, and the provision of multiple ecosystem services. It aims to support forest management approaches capable of responding to ecological change, disturbance risks, and evolving environmental, economic, and societal demands.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, silvicultural systems and management approaches supporting resilient and multifunctional forests; sustainable harvesting and wood mobilisation methods; monitoring, assessment and planning tools for adaptive management; integration of forest genetic resources into management strategies; operational, digital and technical innovations; risk reduction and adaptation strategies; and trade-offs and synergies between ecosystem services.
 TOPIC 3 – Timber and Innovative Wood-Based Products: “How wood is transformed into innovative products” 
 This topic supports research and innovation on the development, performance, and uptake of timber and innovative wood-based products contributing to decarbonisation and the circular bioeconomy. It aims to advance the development and market uptake of sustainable wood-based products and systems, supporting the substitution of fossil-based and carbon-intensive materials and contributing to low-carbon construction and manufacturing.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, engineered timber and timber construction systems; high-value wood-based products, chemicals and materials; substitution of fossil-based and other carbon-intensive materials; more sustainable alternatives to polluting wood treatments and processing practices; standardisation, testing and certification; circular and resource-efficient use of wood-based products; innovative use of underutilised softwood and hardwood species; innovative manufacturing technologies; and approaches to increase market demand and consumer acceptance and uptake.

Our Strategic Innovation Open Call aims to support our mission and vision by investing in innovative solutions, products and services that respond to the most pressing urban mobility challenges. cascade.org: GroundWork Open Call
cascade.projectName: Regenerative living labs to improve soil ecosystem functions by adapting agricultural land use with livestock integration
cascade.furtherInfo:
The GroundWork Project "Regenerative living labs to improve soil ecosystem functions by adapting agricultural land use with livestock integration" addresses a critical environmental and economic challenge: currently, 60-70% of soils in the EU are degraded due to climate change and unsustainable agricultural practices, costing the EU an estimated €50 billion annually. Because intensive livestock farming is a major driver of this degradation, GroundWork aims to catalyse the transformation of the European livestock and agricultural sector.
 A central pillar of GroundWork's strategy is the use of Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) , which is designed to directly involve farmers in the Living Labs and minimize the economic risks of dedicating their land to experimentation. The project will distribute FSTP funding to 75 regenerative farming projects in total. 42 initial experimental sites have been pre-selected to immediately launch the LLs operations, while up to 33 additional farming projects will be engaged through the GroundWork Open Call. 
 Find more information at:
 https://opportunities.getonepass.eu/open-opportunities/groundwork-farms
 https://groundwork-project.eu/
 GroundWork will support up to 33 Farming Projects in this Open Call, distributed:
 ● PT LL – up to 7 Farming Projects 
 ● DE LL – up to 5 Farming Projects 
 ● BE LL – up to 7 Farming Projects 
 ● RS LL – up to 7 Farming Projects 
 ● SE LL – up to 7 Farming Projects 
 The total budget available for this Open Call is EUR 891.000,00 (EUR 27.000,00 per Farming Project).

records.description:
Our 3-year Regenerative Grazing Programme is designed to help farmers improve their farm's soil and environment by changing how their animals feed on the land (so-called "adaptive livestock management"). By joining this Regenerative Grazing Programme, farmers will become part of a local network of farmers and experts where they can share ideas, compare results, and learn from each other's experiences.
 The overall objective of the Programme is to encourage Farmers to actively engage in regenerative farming , through simplicity, continuous guidance, access to finance & business consultation and data-driven communication.
 The main activity expected from the Farming Projects is the implementation of Regenerative Livestock Grazing Practices based on regional farming realities and contexts.
 Other activities:
 - Soil health assessment.
- Pervasive soil health monitoring using sensors.
- Animal welfare assessment.
- Environmental performance assessment (Environmental Life Cycle Assessment￾ELCA).
- Social impact assessment.
- Sharing expertise, ideas exchange, and RLGPs co-design.
 The Programme is divided into 3 main stages over the 36 months. Farmers will receive their grant in installments upon the successful completion of each stage.

 This pilot develops and demonstrates Dynamic Hydrogen Releasers (DHR), based on Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carrier (LOHC) technology. This innovation supports safe and efficient transport, storage, and on-demand release of hydrogen, contributing to Europe’s green mobility and industrial decarbonisation strategies. Throughout the development phase, this pilot needs to define the technical requirements and dimensions of the DHR units . 
 4. Cost-efficient hydrogen transportation cylinders – Udine, Italy 
 This pilot develops composite designs for cost-efficient hydrogen transportation cylinders. The focus is on improving vessel designs to enhance the mobility of energy storage, reducing costs while ensuring the safe and efficient transport of compressed hydrogen.
 5. Gasification plant for waste materials – Zagreb, Croatia 
 This pilot focuses on developing a prototype gasification plant for waste materials. The universal gasification system is designed to process municipal solid waste (MSW) and convert it into valuable products such as synthesis gas (syngas) and charred residue (ash), which can be further used.

records.description:
Activities that can be funded 
 Activities need to be coherent with EU priorities defined by the I3 call and must contribute to NACHIP objectives.
 In line with the objectives of the I3 Programme, the Financial support in the NACHIP will be used for testing, validation, and demonstration of solutions in the field of hydrogen technologies and integration into real-world applications.
 Three main areas of intervention have been identified for the sub-projects funded with the FSTP :
 - Input : innovative chemicals/materials for the NACHIP pilot testing
- Process : solutions to optimize hydrogen-related processes used in the NACHIP pilots
- Output : applications of new technologies complementing the NACHIP value chains: mobility, urban, and manufacturing sectors
 Sub-project proposed in these three main areas may focus on (non-exhaustive list):
 - Prototype development : demonstrating the feasibility of proposed hydrogen technologies.
- Integration into existing infrastructure : scaling the technology for real-world applications.
- Innovation : novel solutions related to hydrogen energy storage, transport, or utilization.
 A non-exhaustive list of potential activities that can be included in the sub-projects presented by the FSTP beneficiaries is reported in the following:
 - trial and testing activities;
- market analysis linked;
- the acquisition and testing of materials;
- integration in the pilots of the SME’s solutions, demonstration in real/operational environment, small and/or medium scale;
- exploitation activities in new application sectors (cross-fertilisation);
 Please to know better on activities that can be funded, check the Technical annex on the main web page.

records.description:
The scope of the I3FLOAT 1 st Open Call is to fund SMEs with proposed innovations in the field of Floating Offshore Wind and proposing a technological solution to one of the challenges posed by the I3FLOAT project. The support scheme aims to fund projects that are relatively close to commercialisation. The expected current TRLs for projects funded under the support scheme are TRL 6-8.
 Applicants to the 1 st Open Call should propose a project that is in line with the different challenges the I3FLOAT project has identified. These challenges can be Open Challenges , which means solutions that are aligned with any of the innovation lines prioritised in the Strategic Innovation Agenda, or Specific Challenges , more concrete and defined by a Challenge Owner.
 Open Challenges refers to innovations that are aligned with the 44 prioritised innovation lines identified in the Floating Wind Strategic Innovation Agenda in areas such as Floating substructures, mooring systems and dynamic cables; Electrical infrastructure and grid connection; Wind turbine, tower or alternative supporting structures and FOW-specific control; Industrialisation; Logistics and offshore installation; Operation, Maintenance and Decommissioning . Further detail is available in the Annex 1 of the Submission Toolkit.
 Specific Challenges are related to specific sectoral needs proposed by so-called Challenge Owners. Examples would be the challenge "Single-pass welding outside for local FOWT serial assembly" proposed by I3FLOAT partner Eolink or " Logistic optimization on the transport of offshore wind structures " proposed by I3 Board member Navantia Seanergies. The list of the 11 Specific Challenges is available in Annex 2 of the Submission Toolkit.

This open call aims to support European SMEs operating in the Mobility, Transport and Automotive ecosystem to redefine their manufacturing or industrial processes, carrying out improvements in current operations and/or incorporating new methods or systems which allow them to be more digital, green and resilient. The call is split into two cut-offs or application periods: the 1st one, launched on the 13th May 2026, will be opened for 2 months, while the 2nd one is expected to be launched in May 2027
 Eligible candidates 
 The Open call is addressed to SMEs working in the MTA ecosystem and located in EU Member States or SMP associated countries. SMEs can apply individually or in consortium (2-3 SMEs from different NUTS2 regions)
 Submission process 
 Applications to the RESIST II process innovation open call must be submitted electronically vía the following online platform . Eligible candidates must fill in the corresponding application form and upload the required annexes (resilience check + declaration of honour)
 Evaluation process in three stages 
 - Verification of the admissibility and eligibility of applications
- Analysis of eligible proposals by at least 3 independent experts and scoring according to the 4 evaluation criteria specified in the Guide for applicants. Applications will then be ranked in descending order based on the scores obtained and the established tie-breaking rules
- The resulting ranking list must be reviewed by the consortium partners for its validation

Achieving this goal is possible thanks to identifying and supporting initiatives that foster integrated local development, with particular emphasis on sustainable development, striving to create more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable local communities. 
 Common values and principles: Project Promoters, Partners and projects shall respect the values and principles governing the implementation of the Norwegian Financial Mechanism, as referred to in Article 1.3.1 of the Regulation, i.e. human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and the respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. Applicants shall describe how gender equality considerations are integrated into the project.
 The strategic role of cities and polycentrism: the call is aimed at towns, with the aim of strengthening their role as drivers of regional growth. By implementing comprehensive and forward-looking development projects that establish modern standards and ensure access to essential services, the Programme aims to secure a territorially balanced, polycentric model of national development.
 Thematic scope of projects: Projects should constitute a coherent response to development challenges and address key aspects related to local/ regional development. This call aims to identify and support initiatives that foster integrated local development, with a particular emphasis on sustainable development, striving to create more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable communities. Projects should address the following aspects, directly (or indirectly) connected with the goals of national midterm development strategy e.g.: economy, spatial policy, transport solutions, public services, integrated city management and institutional development. These projects are intended to empower above mentioned cities to serve as engines for regional growth and secure polycentric territorial development across Poland.
 Project promoters should design projects based on their role as urban functional areas. They may partner with surrounding local governments whose inhabitants use their infrastructure and services and with cities that are part of their influence area.

records.conditions:
General objective: The main purpose of this call is to address the need for Poland’s transition toward a more innovation-driven economy able to face key urban challenges such as sustainability, mobility and citizen engagement through various Smart City initiatives. These initiatives are particularly important in helping cities manage complex issues, including efficient management of city data, crucial for anticipating and responding to potential crises.
 Common values and principles: Project Promoters, Partners and projects shall respect the values and principles governing the implementation of the Norwegian Financial Mechanism, as referred to in Article 1.3.1 of the Regulation, i.e. human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and the respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. Applicants shall describe how gender equality considerations are integrated into the project.
 Supporting Smart City 4.0 solutions in Polish cities: This call aims to identify and support initiatives implementing the Smart City 4.0 concept in Polish cities -  an urban development model that uses modern information and communication technologies, engages residents in decision-making, and contributes to achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals (at least Goal 11). It also seeks to strengthen local government competences in developing and managing smart cities while addressing cities’ current challenges. 
 Thematic scope of projects : Project Promoters are to implement projects in at least one of the following thematic areas listed in three groups:
 1. Smart Governance - the use of modern governance and participatory tools to support data-driven decision-making and citizen involvement in urban management:
 - Smart shrinkage solutions,
- Data-driven and evidence-based governance,
 - Citizen engagement and participatory tools,
- Inclusive policymaking,
- e-Governance and digital public services,
- Urban innovation spaces,
- Smart cultural initiatives and tourism-supporting activities.
 2. Smart Environment - solutions aimed at improving environmental sustainability and strengthening cities’ resilience to climate change:
 - Renewable energy & energy efficiency,
- Smart water & waste management,
- Urban greenery & vegetation management,
- Smart and sustainable mobility,
- Climate resilience,
- BMS – Building Management Systems,
- Environmental monitoring. 
 3. Smart Technology – the deployment of advanced digital technologies that enhance urban management and the quality of public services:
 - Generative AI,
 - Digital twins and data integration platforms,
- IoT infrastructure and sensor-based management,
- Video sensor technologies,
- RPA – Robotic Process Automation,
- AI-based smart city monitoring,
- Data-driven mobility management,
- Accessibility-enhancing technologies,
- Edge computing technologies.

records.conditions:
General objective: The main objective of this call is to enhance the resilience of Polish cities. Projects shall strengthen the institutional capacity of local governments for resilience development and management, including through targeted training that improves staff competences in modern development standards and ensure access to essential citizen-centred public services.
 Common values and principles: Project Promoters, Partners and projects shall respect the values and principles governing the implementation of the Norwegian Financial Mechanism, as referred to in Article 1.3.1 of the Regulation, i.e. human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and the respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities. Applicants shall describe how gender equality considerations are integrated into the project.
 The strategic role and polycentrism: the call is addressed to cities that perform central functions of national and regional significance in Polish polycentric  network. Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of cities to prevent and withstand threats, respond effectively to crisis situations, and adapt to changing social, economic, environmental, and security conditions. As a general rule, solutions relating to safety and resilience will be developed and tested in larger centres so that the resulting solutions can be recommended to towns with less administrative capacity. In addition, the call aims to leverage the potential of regional cities to develop model resilience initiatives that can subsequently be replicated and implemented in other, smaller urban area. 
 Thematic scope of projects: Enhancement of the resilience of Polish cities will be provided by supporting the development and implementation of integrated, pilot solutions that strengthen preparedness for a wide range of natural, technological and militarian hazards. The call promotes embedding resilience into urban governance, planning, and crisis management in line with national, European, and international frameworks.
 This call aims to identify and support initiatives that improve urban capacities across the emergency management cycle, with a particular focus on prevention and preparedness. Actions supported under the call should apply an all-hazards and whole-of-society approach, fostering cooperation between local authorities, emergency services, civil society, the private sector, and residents.
 The call will prioritize projects with a holistic, cross-sectoral approach that brings together a wide range of stakeholders. This is reflected in the assessment criteria, which reward projects that are based on a robust diagnosis of local challenges; are composed of combination of different activities, are operationally linked to crisis management plans and other relevant strategic documents and include relevant stakeholder groups (including civil society organisations).

The EEA Civil Society Fund in Greece aims to foster a vibrant and resilient civil society that protects and promotes democracy, the rule of law, and human rights.
 Within this framework, the purpose of this Open Call is to contribute to the strengthening of democratic values and the rule of law in Greece by supporting CSOs, media actors and other relevant stakeholders to implement projects that enhance media pluralism, safeguard press freedom and promote information integrity.
 For more information, please consult the Open Call text.
 Eligible Applicants
 Project Promoters: Eligible applicants are Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) legally established in Greece no later than 31 December 2023 . Project Promoters must be able to submit financial data covering the two most recently completed financial years (2024 and 2025) and comply with all eligibility requirements set out in this Open Call. 
 Project Partners:  Projects may be implemented in partnership with up to two Project Partners . Eligible Project Partners may include public or private entities, commercial or non-commercial organisations, CSOs, informal groups and university departments, as specified in the Call. Project Partners must share a common objective with the Project Promoter, actively contribute to the implementation of the project, and have been legally established by 31 December 2024 , with the ability to submit financial data covering one completed financial year (2025) .

The EEA Civil Society Fund in Greece aims to foster a vibrant and resilient civil society that protects and promotes democracy, the rule of law, and human rights.
 Within this framework, the purpose of this Open Call is to strengthen the protection and promotion of human rights, social justice, and non-discrimination in Greece.
 Funded projects are expected to contribute to strengthening human rights protection and promotion in practice, by raising awareness, promoting behavioral and institutional change, and reinforcing civil society’s capacity to monitor, document, and respond to human rights challenges. Supported projects may also include the provision of human-rights related training and capacity building, access to support measures for victims of rights violations, the promotion of access to information and justice, and the active engagement of citizens in human rights issues.  
 This Open Call also includes a budget allocation for Rapid Response Actions. Applications for Rapid Response Actions will be invited through a separate announcement at a later stage, enabling the Programme to respond promptly to urgent and emerging human rights needs.
 For more information, please consult the Open Call text.
 Eligible Applicants
 Large & Medium Projects: Eligible Project Promoters are Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) legally established in Greece by 31 December 2023 . Applicants must be able to submit financial data covering two completed financial years (2024 and 2025) . Large & Medium Projects may be implemented either by a single Project Promoter or in partnership with up to two eligible Project Partners .
 Small Projects: Eligible Project Promoters are small Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) legally established in Greece by 31 December 2024 , with the ability to submit financial data covering one completed financial year (2025) . Small Projects are reserved exclusively for small CSOs, defined under this Call as organisations with a total annual revenue (taxable and non-taxable) of less than €80,000 in 2025 , and must be implemented by a single Project Promoter without Project Partners .
 Rapid Response Action Grants: Eligible Project Promoters are Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) legally established in Greece by 31 December 2024 , with the ability to submit financial data covering one completed financial year (2025) . records.conditions:
The Call for Civic Education Projects aims to strengthen democratic values, the rule of law and civic engagement through high-quality civic education programmes and projects. The Call supports initiatives that provide citizens with the knowledge, skills, confidence and concrete opportunities needed to actively participate in democratic life and contribute to inclusive, participatory and resilient communities.
 The Call places particular emphasis on civic education as a lifelong and participatory process that goes beyond the simple transfer of information. Supported projects are expected to connect civic learning with meaningful participation, democratic practice, community engagement, public dialogue, local initiatives and intercultural cooperation. Projects should contribute to stronger democratic competences, better understanding of human rights, the rule of law and democratic processes, and create opportunities for participants to apply what they have learned in practice.
 The Call is implemented through two complementary funding streams . LOT 1 supports the scaling, adaptation, transferability and evaluation of established civic education programmes with demonstrated results, with the aim of expanding their reach and use and strengthening the evidence base for their further development and wider adoption. 2027 European Prize for Women Innovators: Apply now!
 Opportunity
 02/09/2026 10.00 - CET 
 01/12/2026 17.00 - CET 
 EIT
 Are you a woman entrepreneur driving change through innovation?  
 The 2027 European Prize for Women Innovators is your chance to gain European recognition for the impact of your work and inspire the next generation of innovators.   
 Jointly awarded by the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT) and the European Innovation Council (EIC) , the prize celebrates women behind groundbreaking innovations and successful businesses across Europe. It shines a spotlight on leaders who are turning bold ideas into real-world solutions, while helping to close the gender gap in innovation.   
 Across Europe, women innovators are transforming bold ideas into solutions that improve lives and strengthen our societies. Their creativity, courage and determination are not only driving progress in every field, but they are also opening new possibilities for future generations. Through the European Prize for Women Innovators, we celebrate these exceptional women for a more innovative and equal Europe. 
 Ekaterina Zaharieva, Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation   
 Why apply?   
 Winning – or even being recognised – can raise your profile, open up new opportunities and showcase your journey to a Europe-wide audience. The prize honours women innovators whose work is creating value for society, the economy and the planet.   
 How to apply?   
 If you meet the criteria outlined in the Rules of the Contest , submit your application through the Funding & Tenders Opportunities portal for the relevant prize category:   
 - EIC Women Innovators category     
 - EIC Rising Innovators category     
 - EIT Women Leadership category     
 Prize categories   
 In 2027, the prize will be awarded in three categories:   
 - Women Innovators: For women founders and co-founders from the EU and countries associated with Horizon Europe. Prizes: €100 000, €70 000 and €50 000.   
 - Rising Innovators: For promising women innovators under the age of 35. Prizes: €50 000, €30 000 and €20 000.   
 - EIT Women Leadership: For exceptional EIT Community members whose innovation and leadership are making a strong impact. Prizes: €50 000, €30 000 and €20 000.   
 Key dates   
 - Applications open: 2 September 2026    
 - Information session: 17 September 2026, 11.00 CEST – Register here   
 - Deadline to apply: 1 December 2026, 17.00 CEST    
 - Award ceremony: second quarter of 2027   
 Celebrating innovation with impact   
 The European Prize for Women Innovators recognises the women who are shaping Europe’s future through creativity, leadership and entrepreneurship. From deep tech and digital innovation to health, climate and beyond, the prize showcases innovators whose ideas are delivering tangible results and inspiring others to follow.   
 If you are leading an innovative company and ready to take your work to the next level, this is the moment

EIT Culture & Creativity Innovation Projects Open Call
 Opportunity
 25/09/2026 11.00 - CET 
 30/10/2026 17.00 - CET 
 EIT
 The call targets startups, scale-ups and SMEs in three of Europe’s most strategically important creative sectors: fashion, architecture and audiovisual media. Up to 11 projects will be funded in the implementation phase, with up to €900,000 available per project. 
 Thematic priorities for the call include circular textile technologies, bio-based building materials, and responsible AI for content creation, alongside other innovations directly relevant to the EU’s green, digital and social transition goals. 
 From validated innovation to market and scale 
 Focused on market validation, pilot deployment and scaling, the programme supports innovations entering the programme at TRL 7, where a system prototype has been demonstrated in an operational environment, and progressing to TRL 9, where the actual system is proven in an operational environment. 
 The call runs in two stages, allowing both applicants and EIT Culture & Creativity to build evidence before committing to full implementation: 
 - Stage 1 : A single company submits a concept proposal. Selected applicants receive €20,000 to develop a full Business Development Plan, strengthen market and customer validation, define the go-to-market pathway and assess the financing required for implementation and scale, including external investment where relevant. 
- Stage 2 : The strongest plans proceed to a full implementation phase of up to 18 months, with funding of up to €900,000 per project to execute the go-to-market plan, accelerate market adoption and prepare the solution for scale. 
 Access to EIT Culture & Creativity's pan-European ecosystem – industry partners, customers, investors and distribution networks across 30+ countries – is central to how selected projects enter the market. The programme provides high-level matchmaking to connect companies with customers, investors and strategic partners, as well as commercial visibility through Demo Days and the network's flagship Innovation Forum. Where relevant, support will also be provided to connect companies with external capital and strengthen investment readiness. 
 Who can apply 
 This call is open to legal entities established in an eligible country under Horizon Europe – EU Member States (including outermost regions), linked Overseas Countries and Territories, Horizon Europe Associated Countries, or certain low- and middle-income countries – unless otherwise specified in the call guidelines. Third countries associated to Horizon Europe must already be formally associated by the launch time of the calls. 
 Applications close on 30 October 2026 for stage 1 and on 15 March 2027 for stage 2. The stage 2 application form will be made available to applicants selected following stage 1. 
 Full eligibility criteria, timelines and application details are available here

EIT Regional Innovation Booster – Hungary Edition 2027
 Opportunity
 15/09/2026 11.00 - CET 
 30/10/2026 17.00 - CET 
 EIT
 Hungary is the third country to launch a dedicated edition of the EIT Regional Innovation Booster.  
 Delivered jointly by the Hungarian National Innovation Agency (NIÜ), Hungary's national body for innovation policy, and the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), the 2027 edition offers a structured, two-phase market-access programme exclusively for Hungarian companies. 
 A single cohort of eight companies will share EUR 20 000 in EIT funding, alongside a Buddy-led market entry programme and expert mentoring, to enter and scale in a chosen European market. 
 The Hungary 2027 edition is exclusively open to Hungarian start-ups and scale-ups – apply before 15 October 2026. 
 Eligibility criteria 
 - A for-profit SME (per the EU definition), legally registered in Hungary 
- At least 3 full-time employees (FTEs) at the time of application 
- Must own the IPR or hold full exploitation rights to the solution to be taken abroad 
 Technology & traction 
 - A novel product, service, technology or deep tech solution 
- Demonstrated product-market fit in Hungary and proven commercial traction 
 Eligible sectors 
 Climate, Digital, Food & Agritech, Healthcare, Energy and Renewables, Raw Materials, Urban Mobility, or Culture & Creativity. 
 What You receive 
 - 20 hours of 1:1 expert mentoring (Phase 1) and 40 hours with a matched EIT RIB Buddy (Phase 2) 
- A EUR 2 500 lump-sum travel and conference grant (EUR 20,000 total funding allocated to this Call, across all eight companies) 
- International matchmaking and access to the wider EIT Community

Skills-based Continuous Professional Development (CPD) courses Open Call
 Opportunity
 20/07/2026 14.00 - CET 
 30/10/2026 17.00 - CET 
 Creativity
 EIT Culture & Creativity launches EUR 600 000 in funding for skills-based training in the Audio-Visual Media sector
 The Audio-Visual Media (AVM) sector is undergoing rapid technological, market, and regulatory change, creating urgent new skills needs across areas such as artificial intelligence, intellectual property, and digital storytelling.
 EIT Culture & Creativity has launched an open call for proposals supporting the development and delivery of skills-based Continuous Professional Development (CPD) courses for Europe’s AVM sector – designed to help professionals and organisations adapt to these shifts, strengthen workforce resilience, and remain competitive.
 The call funds shorter, targeted training offers designed to help professionals quickly upskill or reskill in response to emerging industry needs. Crucially, the call supports organisations that are ready to rapidly develop and deploy practical, market-relevant learning opportunities through primarily online, flexible training designed for working professionals.
 The call prioritises three specific focus areas addressing key structural and technological shifts in the sector:
 - The first focus area, Intellectual Property, Rights & Content Exploitation, supports training related to advanced rights management, licensing, and value creation in increasingly platform-driven and AI-mediated environments.
- The second, Artificial Intelligence in Audiovisual Production and Workflows, focuses on applied skills for integrating AI into content development, production, post-production, and distribution processes in responsible and competitive ways.
- The third focus area, Storytelling for Digital, Interactive and Cross-Media Environments, supports advanced narrative approaches for immersive, interactive, and platform-based storytelling formats.
 Selected projects can receive up to EUR 75 000 in funding to design and pilot new skills-based training offers, with a total call budget of EUR 600 000. Courses are expected to be available for learners to follow at their own pace, fully online, and delivered in English to support working professionals across Europe.
 A dedicated information session will take place on 30 July, offering prospective applicants the opportunity to learn more and ask questions directly to the team.

New Ventures in Creative Tech (Spark)
 Opportunity
 05/10/2026 09.00 - CET 
 16/11/2026 17.00 - CET 
 EIT
 EIT Culture & Creativity has opened the New Ventures in Creative Tech (Spark) call, offering up to €30 000 per team alongside a nine-month venture-creation programme for early-stage founders. 
 What does the programme offer? 
 The first cohort focuses on tech-centric ventures in Materials & Built Environment, spanning fashion, architecture, and advanced and circular materials. The programme is aimed at founders who are already testing, building and validating a creative tech concept and are ready to turn it into a viable venture. 
 Selected founders kick off with an in-person CreaTech Startup Sprint, a bootcamp hosted in a European city where they work on problem–solution fit alongside international experts, coaches and peer founders. This is followed by a nine-month online venture-creation journey, with coaching, mentoring and topic workshops led by international industry and business experts. Exclusive technology partnerships support venture development, while access to major European events provides visibility. 
 Who can apply? 
 The call is open to early-stage founders – individuals and small multidisciplinary teams – with an innovative business concept, no registered company and the ambition to build for-profit, scalable, tech-centric ventures within the CCSI. Applicants must be based in an EU Member State or a Horizon Europe associated country. 
 Future programmes 
 Future programmes will expand to additional sectors, with details to follow. 
 How to apply 
 Applications close on 16 November 2026 at 17:00 CET. Full eligibility criteria, timelines and application details are available here.

 Opportunity
 23/12/2025 10.00 - CET

 Mobility
 EIT Urban Mobility designed this call to strengthen Europe’s capacity to innovate and tackle pressing urban mobility challenges. 
 By funding early-stage ventures , EIT Urban Mobility aim to stimulate the growth of pre-seed, seed, and Series A companies , amplify the impact of EIT funded research and innovation activities, and foster collaboration across industry, academia, cities, and startups. The initiative supports the development of high-impact solutions that reduce congestion, lower carbon emissions, improve safety and security, and enhance accessibility, while ensuring de-risked, high-quality investment opportunities aligned with the EIT Urban Mobility Financial Support thesis. 
 EIT Urban Mobility will provide financial support of up to €2.5 million per company, for startups developing breakthrough mobility solutions. The purpose of this document is to invite eligible companies to apply for this financial support. Funding is provided through an open application process with multiple cut offs throughout 2026 (see call manual for the cut-off dates in 2027 and 2028):
 - Cut off 1 – 23 February 2026
- Cut off 2 – 18 May 2026
- Cut off 3 – 31 August 2026
- Cut off 4 – 16 November 2026
 What is the Call About?
 To accelerate the transition to sustainable mobility in cities, this Call focuses on five sectors in which Europe has the potential to innovate and create impact. Proposals may target one or more of these sectors, particularly where there are clear synergies between them, for example, applying data-driven solutions and AI to the public sector, or integrating electrification into urban logistics.
 - Urban logistics
- Shared mobility and public transport
- Mobility data management
- Electrification of transport and alternative fuels
- Health and mobility.
 In the future, this call may also include specific topic scopes to address key market opportunities or urgent market failures that can be addressed through our funding.
 EIT Urban Mobility is committed to fostering a more equitable, diverse and inclusive innovation ecosystem. Proposals with diverse teams and clear strategies for inclusive innovation will be positively assessed during the evaluation phase.

SME Market Expansion Open Call 2027
 Opportunity
 09/10/2026 10.00 - CET 
 01/12/2026 17.00 - CET 
 Mobility
 The EIT Urban Mobility is thrilled to launch the new edition of the SME Market Expansion Open Call. 
 The Call is designed to promote business growth and market expansion, encouraging the replication and scaling of successful solutions in new regions or sectors. It offers a strategic platform for SMEs with ambitions to scale by expanding into new markets.
 The Call focus is on accelerating the market uptake of impactful innovations by reducing the risk of development and deployment. EIT Urban Mobility aims to support solutions with a clear path to market, helping cities and businesses confidently procure and scale proven innovations. Through collaboration with an end-client, SMEs can validate their offering in a real-world setting, while gaining visibility and credibility in the European market.
 The Call will focus on five topics:
 - Public and Shared Transport
- Urban Logistics
- Electrification of transport and alternative fuels
- Mobility data management
- Health and mobility
 EIT funding allocation
 The total estimated funding allocated to this Call is €600 000. Around 10 projects are to be implemented by 10 different SMEs. Each awarded entity will receive a fixed lump sum grant of EUR 60 000.
 Who can apply?
 This Call is a mono-beneficiary call addressed to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that are supported by an end client, a public or private entity, committed to testing and demonstrating the solution.
 To ensure a balanced portfolio of projects, SMEs selected for the previous SME Market Expansion Open Call 2026 are not eligible to apply for this Call.
 Info session
 Info webinar and contact details are available to guarantee the maximum support to the applicants during the proposal’s preparation process.
 To help applicants with the preparation and submission of their proposals, EIT Urban Mobility will host one live Call info webinar focused on the Call content, calendar, scope, topics, KPIs, the submission and evaluation tools and procedures, end-client role, and the financial aspects including contribution to EIT Urban Mobility financial sustainability.
 Info webinar: 15 October 2026 10.00 – 11.00 CET. Register and watch on Zoom .

EIT Higher Education Initiative Call for Proposals 2026
 Opportunity
 20/10/2026 11.00 - CET 
 13/01/2027 17.00 - CET 
 EIT
 The EIT Higher Education Initiative Call is now open!
 The call is offering up to €1.25 million per project over 18 months, with a total budget of €40 million, to strengthen innovation and entrepreneurship capacity in higher education, focusing on manufacturing and deep tech. It will support projects that help universities develop innovation and entrepreneurship skills, improve technology transfer services and build stronger links with businesses. 
 Projects will focus on three key areas: 
 - STEM talent for innovation and entrepreneurship: Developing innovation, entrepreneurship and intellectual property skills among students and staff in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) and related fields. 
- Institutional capacity for knowledge valorisation and innovation: Strengthening universities' ability to turn research and knowledge into innovations, including through improved technology transfer, intellectual property management and support for startups. 
- Integration into innovation ecosystems: Building stronger links between higher education institutions, businesses, research organisations, investors and innovation networks, particularly in manufacturing and deep tech. 
 Eligibility and consortium requirements 
 Who can apply?
 To be eligible, consortia must meet the following requirements:
 - Consortium composition: Each consortium must include at least five funded partners: at least three HEIs (from three different Horizon Europe-eligible countries, including at least one EU Member State) and at least two business/industry partners and/or business/industry representative organisations (e.g. SMEs, startups, larger enterprises and industry associations). Industry partners operating in manufacturing or deep-tech technologies are strongly encouraged to join a consortium. 
- Eligibility: Organisations funded under the EIT HEI Call 2025 are not eligible to apply under the 2026 call. Each organisation may participate as a funded beneficiary in only one 2026 call application. 
 How to apply 
 Consortia of higher education institutions, businesses, research organisations, public bodies and other non-academic partners can prepare their applications by consulting the full  call text   and finding potential partners through the  matchmaking platform . 
 Selected projects will be announced later in 2027.
